about: What T2.8c's multi-call cases (contract/cases/s1/multicall.*.json, main's 1fc5a686) give beside their observation lines, by case key, recorded from the reference's public calls: the rows each call scores, the result through to_pandas() (every row, or both ends of a long one), and a refusal's details, the answers carried on it (details answered), its first sentence and, for a call past the 30 MiB body, the remedy the client names. contract/tests/test_t28c_multicall.py holds python-core to them, observed by the same code (observe).

multicall.body-30mib.one-row.remedy: A call already scores one row, so there is no smaller one to ask for: what comes down is num_context_samples, num_neighbors or the columns the graph carries.

multicall.body-30mib.one-row@postgres.remedy: A call already scores one row, so there is no smaller one to ask for: what comes down is num_context_samples, num_neighbors or the columns the graph carries.

multicall.body-30mib.one-row@sqlite.remedy: A call already scores one row, so there is no smaller one to ask for: what comes down is num_context_samples, num_neighbors or the columns the graph carries.

multicall.body-30mib.several-rows.remedy: What comes down is one of three. For an ordinary question it is the call: materialize(rows_per_call=N) below the 3 this one holds asks for the same entities in more and smaller calls. Where the context is itself over the limit, no call is small enough, and it is num_context_samples, num_neighbors or the columns the graph carries. For a ranking or a forecast, which is one call per candidate or step and is never batched, it is the entities.
